params._closeTime: Unix timestamp after which buy() is disabled.
params._creationDeposit: Amount of MON locked in this contract, refunded on resolve.
params._creator: Address to refund the creation deposit; address(0) = no refund.
params._isDemo: If true, time-lock is bypassed and Pyth window uses block.timestamp.
params._pythPriceFeedId: Pyth price feed ID to query on resolution.
params._resolveTime: Unix timestamp after which resolve() is callable                         (ignored when isDemo == true).

claim().notice: Winners claim their proportional share of the pool minus the resolver bounty. Payout formula (CEI pattern):   effectivePool = totalPool - resolverBounty   payout = userWinShares * effectivePool / winningPoolBalance The bounty reduction is proportional: winners and losers each contribute BOUNTY_BPS / 10_000 of their pool to the resolver reward.

getPrices().notice: Returns each outcome's implied probability as a fraction of 1e18.

resolve(bytes[]).notice: Anyone can resolve this market. For regular markets: callable only after resolveTime. For demo markets (isDemo == true): callable at any time; the Pyth VAA window is anchored to block.timestamp so a fresh price update is always valid. On successful resolution:   1. Resolver earns a bounty (0.5% of pool, max 1 MON).   2. Creator receives their creation deposit back.   3. winningOutcome is set; winners may call claim().

resolverBounty().notice: Bounty paid to the resolver on resolution; subtracted from effective pool in claim() payouts so that total claimable == totalPool - resolverBounty.

thresholds(uint256).notice: One element for binary markets; N elements for CLOSEST_TO (band midpoints). All values normalised to Pyth expo = -8 (USD × 1e8).
